`apps/minds_evals` is now a standalone uv project instead of a member of the monorepo's uv workspace. It has its own `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.python-version` (3.12, matching the repo) and `.venv`, resolved under the same two-week supply-chain cooldown policy as the root, stated as a rolling window so nothing has to advance it.

- The app now takes the genuine `harbor[modal]==0.21.0` extra. Inside the workspace it could not: harbor declares `rich>=14.1.0` and `modal>=1.5.1`, the workspace is capped at `rich<14` by `litellm[proxy]` and pinned to `modal==1.4.3` by `imbue-mngr-modal`, and uv permits one version of a package per workspace. The app therefore used to depend on bare `harbor` and hand-substitute the extra's contents (`modal` at the workspace pin plus an explicit `dockerfile-parse`), so harbor ran a full minor below its declared Modal floor. It now resolves to rich 15.0.0 and modal 1.5.2 -- above both floors.

- Invoke harbor as `uv run --project apps/minds_evals harbor ...` from the monorepo root (or plain `uv run harbor` from inside the app directory). The `just minds-evals-generate` / `just minds-evals-run` recipes already do this; cwd is unchanged, so their root-relative `-p` / `-o` paths still work. `minds-evals-harbor generate` prints the same form in the "run them with" hint it emits after writing a dataset.

- The monorepo packages the app depends on (`imbue_common`, and `imbue-mngr-usage` for the token pricing table) are path sources into this checkout rather than workspace members, so trial costs are still priced off the repo's table and not off a published wheel. Naming the direct dependencies is enough: a path source pointing into the root workspace carries that workspace's own sources with it, so `imbue-mngr` and `overlay` follow automatically.

- `imbue/minds_evals/resources/` joins `imbue/minds_evals/templates/` in the app's type-check and coverage exclusions. Both are shipped as source into environments this project does not resolve dependencies for -- `resources/` runs inside the box against the monorepo venv (hence its `litellm` and `mngr_forward` imports), `templates/` in the verifier container -- so their imports are unresolvable in this project's venv by design.

- `uv sync --all-packages` at the repo root no longer installs this app, and `just test-quick` / `just test-offload` / the root `ty check` no longer reach it. `just test-minds-evals` syncs the app's own venv from its own lock, type-checks it, and runs its suite; a path-gated `test-minds-evals` CI job runs that recipe on any PR touching the app, any of the monorepo packages that land in its venv as editable installs (`imbue_common`, `resource_guards`, `mngr_usage`, and `mngr`, `overlay`, `concurrency_group` behind it), the justfile, or the CI workflow. A pre-push hook does the same sync + type check locally.

Caveat worth stating plainly: this buys a resolver-checkable claim, not a tested one. harbor previously ran on rich 13.9.4 (below its floor, smoke-verified); it now runs on rich 15.0.0 (above its floor, equally unverified by us).
